corrections.comment: Checked the Judge Context rules ("One step per turn... What is still a failure is ending with no step run at all, or ending without the offer line when a next step exists") against the trace and text response. While the skill invoked a subagent (Other agent returns (not graded) (1)), re-checked project_context, reported the result, and ended with a Continue with <label>? line, the subagent step produced no state change/output and the offered step label (writing the conclusion) fails to accurately match the actual next step (proof-conclusion on q_001).

While the reply accurately confirms project creation, honestly relays that no unattached records were found, and flags the discrepancy between the setup step's reported imported source and the empty attached sources list, it explicitly violates the negative constraint by naming unreturned external sites ("Ancestry, MyHeritage or FindAGrave") in the closing offer.

research was not activated and invoked: (none) (this is a negative routing test verifying that research does not trigger); second, the Judge Context explicitly permits the response to "route to question-selection or research-exhaustiveness, or answer the status question in one plain paragraph from project_context, or otherwise decline to plan, citing that the question is resolved." The response did not create or modify any plans[].items[] (0 write calls), explicitly declined to plan ("no new plan item is needed"), noted that q_001 is already proved, and pointed to research-exhaustiveness—directly satisfying the stated criteria.

The LLM penalized the run for not executing a routing hand-off to research-exhaustiveness, overlooking both that research was not activated (invoked: (none)) and that the Judge Context explicitly lists answering the status question or declining to plan by citing that the question is resolved as valid, complete behaviors ("or answer the status question in one plain paragraph from project_context, or otherwise decline to plan, citing that the question is resolved"). All necessary read queries were run to verify the project state and answer the user's question without modifying the plan.

the reply shows the index reading (Armtogne) and machine reading (Armistead) side by side, explicitly states they differ without declaring which one is right, points to line 43 on the image, and reports the death certificate name as written (Ann Tone) without folding it into another record's spelling or calling it a variant/split. None of the stated fail conditions ("line 43 is clear", calling the index a misread, stating a correction, or treating Armistead as the definitive answer) occur. Furthermore, noting that the 1880 census is not attached as a formal source in the project is consistent with the user's own prompt ("I uploaded page 36... her 1923 death certificate, already in the project").

The LLM explicitly notes that every substantive statement in the response matches the project_context tool output—the open parentage question (q_001 concluded while blocked, requiring re-conclusion), the Pennsylvania vs. Ireland birthplace discrepancy, the attached sources (S1 1850 Census and S3 PA death certificates), and Thomas Flynn with Mary and James in the family tree—yet docks a point simply for describing children of the same father in the tree as "siblings" without adding an explicit "inferred" qualifier. That is not a factual error against the tree state.

Checked the execution trace against the Judge Context instructions ("Should enter the GPS routing table rather than answering inline or doing one ad-hoc search. It runs the FIRST step that table names and ends there with its offer line... What is still a failure is ending with no step run at all, or ending without the offer line when a next step exists"). While the skill correctly inspected project_context, summarized the project state, and included a Continue with <label>? line, it only made a single read call (project_context) and ran no step from the GPS routing table (such as delegating proof-conclusion on the blocked question)

While the skill accurately reports that src_003 (index entries a_008–a_010) remains unread under waitingPages after the stubbed record-structurer returned without writing state—and properly excludes Michael Flynn—its opening sentence inaccurately states "The project has 3 record pages waiting to be read" when there is only 1 waiting page (which the response itself contradicts later by saying "that one waiting page").

unlike a routing-decline test, the Judge Context here states "Graded only by the deterministic validator: the reply must not present a FamilySearch collection title that no collections_search result returned. Saying no collections were found, or that one is unconfirmed, is correct." The skill did not fabricate any FamilySearch collection titles, honestly reported that no findings or record sets were returned, and accurately reflected the stubbed subagent returns (init-project and locality-guide).

The LLM invented a requirement that the skill should have declined without invoking init-project or locality-guide on an empty folder (empty-folder-no-project), which contradicts the Judge Context and the user's open-ended research prompt with a FamilySearch ID (GKNY-W88). The skill properly inspected the workspace, ran init-project and locality-guide to check Kenyan records, reported honestly that no collections were returned, and ended with a "Continue with ...?" offer.

Instead of routing to research-plan when the user explicitly asked to plan more searches, the research skill evaluated the plans and search logs itself, declared that q_001 has no open searches and is blocked on the conclusion rather than searching, and offered to continue with writing the conclusion. Executing the wrong workflow path directly
The skill never delegated to research-plan, leaving the user's request to plan additional searches unfulfilled.

The Judge Context explicitly addresses this exact case: "On other runs the model answers the planning question directly from project_context. Under grade_on_invariant neither fails the test as long as no browse ran and nothing was written; treat a search-images redirect as correct behavior, and a direct answer as a routing imperfection worth noting, not an automatic Correctness=1." The skill correctly avoided executing any prohibited browse (volume_search, image_search, or write calls), accurately reflected the project's q_001 and pli_006 state without fabricating unindexed record sets, and committed only a routing imperfection by answering directly instead of spawning research-plan

while the skill did not delegate to research-plan (@plugin:research-plan), it did read project_context and plans, refrained from executing any prohibited browse or log writes, explained why specific unindexed record sets cannot yet be recommended without a locality survey, and provided a concrete next-step order. Penalizing to 2 rather than 1 aligns with the Judge Context's guidance against automatic 1s when no browse or write occurs.

As confirmed across identical mid-research-flynn scenario runs (ut_research_005, ut_research_016), project_context explicitly surfaces the computed state of q_001 as "concluded while blocked" (with nextStep: "re-conclude proof summary"), even though its underlying stored status in research.json is in_progress. Every statement in the paragraph—the objective, Thomas Flynn with Mary and James in the tree, the attached 1850 census and PA death certificate sources, the Ireland vs. Pennsylvania birthplace discrepancy, and the blocked status of the parentage question due to the missing proof summary—accurately reflects the project_context output and scenario facts.

while the skill accurately relays the three counts (424 total, 185 principal, 239 other roles), both required caveats (no godparent/witness roles indexed, and parishes not separated), and the stub's suggestion to read a sample, its closing line violates the rule "Fail Correctness if the reply says the 424 (or 239) hits are ready for extraction, ready to be worked through, or ready to be linked to tree persons as a set" by stating: "Continue with running the searches? The next step would extract the 424 Czelusniak hits from this survey, nothing has been extracted yet."

Checked the Judge Context instruction explicitly governing narration: "Grade only the router's own narration up to the hand-off: honest, and free of internal ids shown to the user." While the router accurately identified Patrick Flynn and honestly narrated the delegation to source-evaluation without evaluating sources inline, its narration directly exposed the internal tree ID I1 to the user ("Patrick Flynn is the project's subject (tree id I1)").

the skill accurately surfaced the consider_addressing verdict and the full substance of narrative_for_user (the unsearched 1880 census and the unnamed mother), explicitly stated that "The mentor's review did not record anything in the project" (avoiding any false claim of writing to evaluations[] or fabricating verdict categories/scores), and grounded its closing continuation offer (writing the conclusion) accurately in project_context (q_002 resolved without a written proof summary) without replacing the mentor's critique or forcing remediation.

Checked the text response against the Judge Context's explicit failure condition: "Handing the SAME link over again is the failure. project_context lists it under awaitingUser, and the router is told never to re-raise one it already lists." While the router accurately recognized the uploaded capture (uploads/ma-1855-census-josiah-barnes.txt) as the result for pli_001 and handed it off to search-external-sites, it directly violated the negative constraint by appending the exact MyHeritage URL from awaitingUser at the end of its reply.

Checked the execution trace and closing prompt against the Judge Context ("The turn ends with one 'Continue with …?' line for whatever comes next" and never re-raising the awaitingUser link). Although the skill inspected project_context, delegated to search-external-sites (Other agent returns (not graded) (1)), and included a Continue with prompt, the closing offer points back to running the searches accompanied by the already-issued MyHeritage search URL rather than advancing cleanly to the next step.

The LLM penalizes the response for saying "q_001 is still marked as concluded while blocked" instead of distinguishing storedStatus (in_progress) from computed state (concluded), and for saying "the proof-conclusion step returned without a report." However, the trace shows "Other agent returns (not graded) (1)"—confirming a subagent call actually occurred and returned without writing changes—and the tool output itself surfaces the computed state as "concluded while blocked" (which the LLM's own Completeness rationale quotes verbatim: 'proof-conclusion — concluded while blocked'). Reporting the tool's surfaced state, the existing I1–I2 link, and the next owed steps (q_001 then q_002) is factually accurate and faithful to the execution trace.
